newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea raises '97 pork export target to 65,000T.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea raises '97 pork export target to 65,000T.

text.p: South Korea raised its pork export target to 65,000 tonnes in 1997 from the previous target of 55,000 tonnes due to an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in Taiwan, the Agriculture Ministry said on Friday.

The ministry said in a statement that it would also raise its export target in 1998 to 90,000 tonnes from the previous target of 60,000 tonnes and in 2001 to 180,000 tonnes from the previous 120,000 tonnes.
By increasing pork exports, South Korea could take 9.7 percent of total Japanese pork imports in 1997 and 26 percent in 2001, it said.
Last year, South Korea took 5.6 percent of total Japanese pork imports.

The statement said the country's pork exports in April rose 43 percent to 4,984 tonnes from 3,477 tonnes a year ago and 2,574 tonnes a month earlier due to the foot-and-mouth disease outbreak in Taiwan.
However, South Korea's pork exports for the first four months fell to 11,457 tonnes from 12,508 tonnes a year ago due to a slowdown in exports before the disease outbreak in Taiwan.
The statement said the country's hog population would reach 711,000 head in 1997, compared to 676,000 head in 1996, and 752,000 head in 2001.
South Korea said it would open its pork market from July of this year. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5651
